ops.title: Shipped-fleet fact: every 'graceful' fusekit fuse teardown has been MNT_FORCE at the syscall — cgofuse FileSystemHost.Unmount's Darwin hostUnmount is literally unmount(mountpoint, MNT_FORCE). Found by gpt-5.5 in the Holder v2 round-3 review (2026-07-11),

ops.body:
Found 2026-07-11 during the Holder v2 (fusekit v1.0.0) review loop; verified by reading the pinned dependency source directly.

**The fact.** `github.com/winfsp/cgofuse@v1.6.1-0.20260531120352-2fa812d1bdc7/fuse/host_cgo.go:745` — `hostUnmount` on Darwin/BSD is `return 0 == unmount(mountpoint, MNT_FORCE);`. fusekit's `Handle.Unmount` (mount.go:198, unchanged from shipped main) called `h.host.Unmount()`, so **every fusekit fuse-path teardown the fleet has ever done — unmount, reclaim, retire sweep, exit sweep, daemon heal churn — was a forced unmount at the kernel**, despite godoc and memories describing v0.22.x+ as "graceful-only teardown" (that release removed force *escalation*, but the single underlying call was itself MNT_FORCE).

**Why it matters.**
- The [[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]] risk model changes: "graceful-only" teardown was never a panic-safety fence on the fuse path; the fleet survived on the *other* mitigations (namedattr=false, quiesced teardown timing). Any pre-v1.0.0 interim operation (manual unmounts, daemon heals on the live fuse-t accounts) is running MNT_FORCE.
- It retro-explains observed behavior: teardowns "succeeding" under sessions that should have EBUSYed, and the daemon unmount-churn incidents ([[claude-pool-nfs-not-responding-diagnosis]]) ripped mounts rather than bouncing busy.
- Review-process lesson: the claim was found by the gpt-5.5 refuter lens reading the PINNED DEPENDENCY source, not the repo diff — dependency-boundary "the comment says graceful" claims must be verified against the vendored implementation.

**Second dimension (round-4 refuter): cgofuse's own signal handler.** cgofuse `Mount` unconditionally creates `host.sigc` (host.go:799) and `hostInit` runs `signal.Notify(sigc, SIGINT, SIGTERM)` (host.go:479); a delivered TERM makes cgofuse's goroutine call `host.Unmount()` = MNT_FORCE — per live mount, no API knob. launchd TERMs every agent at logout/shutdown/`launchctl bootout`, so this fires in real life regardless of runbooks.

**The fix (fusekit v1.0.0, Holder v2 rounds 4-5; user chose Reset-dance over forking cgofuse).** (1) `Handle.Unmount` never calls cgofuse's Unmount; it issues `syscall.Unmount(dir, 0)` (genuinely graceful; EBUSY ⇒ ClassBusy). (2) After mount-ready, fusekit calls `signal.Reset(SIGINT, SIGTERM)` — globally unsubscribing cgofuse's channel — then `Config.ReArmSignals` re-subscribes the holder's own handler. The ordering is deterministic by FUSE protocol, not timing: init is served before any other op, and the readiness probe is a real op through the mount, so a successful probe proves cgofuse's Notify already ran. A source-pin test asserts the pinned module still registers in hostInit, so a future pin that moves registration fails loudly. Force exists only at the holder's two fenced, carcass-proof-v2-gated internal sites.
